svg.title: Speech, as a pipeline of CARDIAC machines
svg.text: Speech, as a pipeline of CARDIAC machines

65 machines: 19 turn text into phonemes, 36 turn phonemes into frame cards and 10 turn frame cards into 8 kHz samples; the largest fills 96 of its 100 cells. The host deals the text and the decks, carries each machine's output cards on to the next, and joins each sample's two values.
FRONT END: PHONEMES TO FRAME CARDS, 36 MACHINES
VOICE BOX: FRAME CARDS TO SAMPLES, 10 MACHINES
ONCE A CHARACTER, THEN ONCE A NUMBER
scan reads the text twice (is it all capitals?), sorts each character by
its row of the ASCII table, and cuts words, numbers and punctuation;
numbers become words, years in pairs
which all-capital words are spelled out, letter by letter by name; the
function words and the hand-written exceptions, looked up in a deck read
ONCE A LETTER, RULE BY RULE
the letter's section of the rule deck; each rule's left and right
contexts tested by two machines, one reading each way through the word;
the first rule that matches gives the phonemes
one of each run of the same consonant; primary stress on a content word's
first full vowel, secondary on the other long ones; boundaries between
an 11-card record for each segment: its code, stress, word start, pause
length, sentence end, and six cards of its row of the phoneme table
run on the records in reverse, so each segment learns what comes after it
in its word: a vowel later, the next vowel's stress, the next sound's
a consonant's stress; Klatt's rules 2 to 11 as lists of factors in
hundredths, multiplied into PRCNT; DUR = (INHDUR - MINDUR) PRCNT / 100 +
ONCE A SEGMENT, THEN ONCE A FRAME
the segment before each one; a summary of each sentence for the pitch;
each frame's place in its segment, in tenths, and the weights of the
130 Hz falling to 100 across the sentence, a rise at stressed vowels, the
fall (85 Hz) or rise (160 Hz) at the end, and the pitch period, 8000 / f0
a stop's closure and burst, aspiration after P T K, each frame's two
target filters blended by its place, the glides at the segment's ends; a
silent frame keeps the filter before it
the filter's gain times a sonorant's loudness, 3 dB down when unstressed,
falling across a vowel, times sqrt(60 P) / 100 so a pulse carries the
frame's power, and a glide's factor from the glide table
each frame as the voice box reads it, a frame behind: V, P, A, K10 to K1
ONCE A FRAME, THEN ONCE A STEP
each value's step to the next frame, (next - this) / 10 by one SFT, none
across a change of voicing; ten steps of 20 samples a frame
each K as two digits, a sign, a
shift and a rounding half (0 in a
a pulse of height A every P
e, or +A and -A from a decimal
five machines of two stages each: f goes down from L1 to L5, each b goes
back up one machine; every multiply is a jump into a row of nine ADDs, an
yd = f + 0.9 yd, kept as thousands and units; out goes 20 yd as two
values, the thousands and then the units
ASCII codes, a card a character, then -1;
ASCII rows, number words, letter names,
the host puts the segment records
each machine dealt the columns of the
records it reads, collated a port
the phoneme table, the filters and the glide factors:
the host joins thousands x 1000 + units
words for the rules; finished words
phonemes as 10 x code, the rules'
words and the finished ones in order
fetched by record number, or read through again and again
what lies ahead of each segment: three decks, A, B and C
the records and A, B, C, a few columns to
each machine of every stage that follows
rows, filters and glide factors fetched by number
5 cards a K, ten to each
two values a sample: thousands, units
